C11-282: remote checks complete; native selection pending

Needs you: nothing during the UI hold. C11-282 remains pending native mouse selection and selection above 1 MiB. This artifact records completed remote checks; it is not an overall PASS.

Candidate main 12d4f21a8822a3a7763d3a26b5295d8f6213c60a, Debug invocation dc3b9a7120b34a03a050f42551f5809c. Earlier clean main b6f239bd077164d2ff2e7aa18d5464d4e885fd35, invocation 273d23384a7a436b8d5d14b81eb6f292, is the permitted comparison substitute while the final C11-270 soak is deferred. Both use engine 5830d1976eecca0d7dee202aef8fb2338d99ed6d. Canonical build and re-signed guest executable identities differ and are recorded separately in the retained build evidence and reports.

The bounded native ownership fixture passed 120 seconds: 1,903,697 iterations, 3,807,394 acquired buffers, exactly as many frees, and tracked native outstanding bytes zero. It exercised forced renderer BUSY, allocation failure and no-selection/invalid contracts. RSS rose from 52,248,576 to 61,325,312 bytes; no universal leak-free or large-selection claim follows from these small-result observations.

The actual packaged read/close probe completed 50 rounds: 23 empty successes and 27 not_found replies. Eighteen not_found reads started before close completed, but none was fully sent before close started. Every post-close target was rejected and selection stayed unchanged. This proves observed overlap and stale-target safety; it does not force main-queue ordering or cancellation of a selected owned buffer. The first wrapper attempt rejected an output path before probing; the corrected second wrapper is the reported run.

The matched stock workload ran 30 real PTY producers at 20 Hz, 100 input receipts and 20 socket-observed workspace switches on each artifact. Both had zero missed probes, no cleanup errors and reaped controllers. The workload and fixture hashes match. No selection call was added to either comparison; the baseline has no selection API. These are socket-synthetic input and switch observations, not hardware key or visible-frame latency. All intervening main changes are present, so isolated ticket attribution is unavailable.

A separate candidate experiment added 100 actual empty-selection reads under the same streaming load. All succeeded with zero selected bytes; 100 capture and 100 worker encode logs were retained, all encode records isMain=false. Caller p95 3.363833 ms, maximum 42.774 ms. Native/copy/worker measurements describe empty results, not native formatting of a large selected buffer. Successful capture still performs native work synchronously on main; the caller deadline cannot preempt it.

Native twenty mouse select/read/read/CLI/clear cycles, screenshot-confirmed word equality and actual retained selection beyond 1 MiB remain pending QUIET WINDOW START. Earlier foreground/geometry and empty-drag attempts remain unresolved evidence, not a regression verdict. No additional UI attempt occurred during the hold.

All raw receipts were retrieved before cleanup. Owned app PIDs were absent, the disposable guest was stopped and deleted, and the completed c11-282 runtime tag was removed. Guest app cleanup used bounded owned PID signals after the known native Quit gate; it is not synthesized dismissal proof. The independent common native smoke proved app-menu Quit. Cleanup free space was 126.505 GB; concurrent fleet writes affect net deltas. Protected caches and foreign files were untouched.
